generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, a good search is planned around the kind of claim you need to support. A question about a well-established effect sends you to textbooks and review articles; a question about a current controversy sends you to recent empirical papers. Deciding the source type and date range before you search is how psychologists avoid drowning in results that were never going to fit the question.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students need sources for the same essay on whether a therapy works, and both begin to search.

Tom opens the discovery service and types the essay title straight in. Thousands of results come back, so he skims the first page and takes whatever looks relevant. There was no objective and no plan, so the search returned everything and nothing.

Amara stops to plan. She decides she needs recent trials and reviews rather than textbook summaries, and sets a date range of the last ten years. Only then does she search, and the first page of results is already close to usable.

Both ran a search. Amara did the thinking before the search, and the plan did most of the work.
generatedProse.summary: Planning a psychology search means deciding, before you type, what claim you need to support and what kind of source will support it. A current controversy needs recent empirical papers; an established effect may rest on reviews or textbooks. You can now set an objective and choose source type and date range for a search of your own. The next lesson builds the keywords that drive it.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Amara do before starting to search?

items.text: She set a clear objective and chose the source type and date range to fit it.
She typed the essay title straight into the search box.
She skimmed the first page of results and took what looked relevant.
She read every result the search returned before choosing.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara planned the search: a clear objective, then a matching source type and date range.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara decided before the search, not during it.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Before searching, Amara set an objective and chose a source type and date range. Typing the title or skimming results is the unplanned approach Tom took.
